newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Plains fed cattle market light at $68-trade.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Plains fed cattle market light at $68-trade.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle trade Wednesday was slow and prices showed signs of weakness, feedlot sources said.
The market was feeling pressure from lower Chicago Mercantile Exchange live cattle futures and sharply lower beef prices, the sources said.
About 2,000 head sold in the Texas Panhandle and western Oklahoma area and about 3,500 in Kansas at $68.00 per cwt, unchanged from Tuesday's large volume.
Beef prices were pressured by increased supplies and ideas retail buying was starting to wind down.
Retailers usually buy two weeks in advance of planned meat promotions and the week before Christmas finds more turkey and ham advertised than beef.
But, retail buying can be extended if prices are discounted enough.
Beef prices at midday were quoted down $2.19 to $2.40 per cwt for choice cuts and down $1.01 to $1.30 for selects, according to USDA. There were 249 fabricated loads sold.
